newsitem.title: UK: Siemens delivers 1st Heathrow Express train.
newsitem.headline: Siemens delivers 1st Heathrow Express train.

text.p: The first of 14 purpose- built 100 miles per hour Heathrow Express trains was delivered to UK airport operator BAA Plc by engineering giant Siemens AG on Monday at a London handover ceremony.

The full train service from London to Heathrow airport is scheduled to start in June 1998, providing a 15 minute connection from London Paddington train station to Heathrow airport. The Heathrow Express service will rival the current connection provided by London Underground's Piccadilly Line and marks a 440 million stg investment by BAA.
From autumn 1997 a FastTrain high speed rail and coach service will serve Heathrow with a journey time of 30 minutes, before the full rail service kicks in the following year.
Sir John Egan, BAA chief executive, called the delivery on Monday "a key step in the history of Heathrow Express." Heathrow is Europe's busiest and biggest airport hub.

Phil Tizzard, group managing director of Siemens Plc, said his company was contracted to carry out maintenance on the trains for the next 10 years. "This is very much a sign of the times, in that provision of rolling stock and the maintenance are becoming inseparable elements of new contracts."
